sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Canadian common law at the federal level; Quebec private law based on the civil law tradition codified in the Civil Code of Quebec), with federal statutory overlay for corporate, securities, and AML/CFT matters.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–China Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (FIPA), in force October 1, 2014
Canada–China Income Tax Agreement (1986), as amended
United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement (USMCA), in force July 1, 2020
Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally in force September 21, 2017

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA); An Act respecting the transparency of enterprises in the exercise of certain enterprise activities, CQLR c. T-31.5 (Quebec UBO register); Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c. S-31.1; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport or national identity document of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the document owner's jurisdiction of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Existence / Good Standing for any corporate UBO or substantial corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country corporate registry or equivalent authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or shareholder register extract identifying directors and shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country corporate registry or registered agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing a Quebec-licensed incorporator or registered office provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: UBO or authorized corporate representative executed before a notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation of all non-French corporate and identification documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: OATIQ-certified translator (Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interprètes agréés du Québec)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP (politically exposed persons) screening under FINTRAC guidance; mandatory screening against Canadian federal sanctions lists issued under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, plus OFAC, UN Security Council, and EU financial sanctions lists. Every UBO, director, and authorized representative must undergo continuous adverse-media and sanctions-list screening at incorporation and annually thereafter; Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) applies to foreign PEPs and persons resident in or transacting with high-risk jurisdictions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire d'entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online services portal, registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11), corporate names in Quebec must be in French. A name in another language may be used only together with a French version; names composed solely of non-French text are inadmissible. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin/French characters according to standard administrative transliteration rules, and the REQ will normalize accents and official Quebec-specific French orthography.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed corporate name, the applicant may, within 30 days of the written REQ notice, submit a written reconsideration request to the Registraire d'entreprises du Québec, including legal arguments and alternative proposed names. If the reconsideration is refused, the applicant may appeal to the Court of Québec (civil division) within 30 days of the reconsideration decision under the Code of Civil Procedure, articles 529–530. The applicant may also submit a new name reservation request at any time without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for this non-regulated B2B marketplace platform industry, provided the registered office is a physical address in Quebec (not a post-office box) where corporate records are kept and legal process may be served during ordinary business hours. Co-working suites and professional registered-office service providers are acceptable under the Business Corporations Act (Quebec). Pure non-staffed virtual addresses do not satisfy the statutory requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 5–10% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the Registraire d'entreprises or provincial verification officials for a low-risk, non-licensed B2B e-commerce entity. The likelihood increases to approximately 25% or greater upon the occurrence of AML/CFT suspicious transaction reports, material tax discrepancies, or non-compliance indicators.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per source page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff and prevailing market benchmark per document

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (CQLR c C-38, ss. 9–29, 36–55, 146–212); Canada Business Corporations Act (R.S.C. 1985, c C-44, ss. 19–29 and 106–118) if federal incorporation is chosen
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), a service of the Ministère des Services gouvernementaux du Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of incorporation (statuts de constitution) filed electronically through the Registraire's incorporation service
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed by the QBCA; shares may be issued for consideration fixed by the directors, and no escrow account is required for a B2B marketplace corporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) The share subscriptions of the incorporator and initial subscribers, as entered in the Share Register, are approved, and the directors shall issue common shares in accordance therewith. (2) The registered office of the Corporation is fixed at the address indicated in the Notice of Registered Office, and the Registrar is authorised to file the same. (3) Until the next annual general meeting, [name] shall serve as President, [name] as Secretary, and [name] as Treasurer. (4) The officers are authorised to open bank accounts, engage professional advisers, and complete all registrations and filings required for the B2B electronic marketplace business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online name search portal (Recherche de nom)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a NUANS/Quebec name search on the Registraire's website. Select a corporate name that is distinctive and compliant with Quebec's language of business requirements. If needed, reserve the name in the Registraire's system prior to filing the articles.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, file a revised name or appeal the refusal by submitting written justification to the Registraire within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of articles of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec electronic filing portal / corporate law counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation (Form A) in compliance with QBCA statutory requirements, including corporate name, registered office, share structure and restrictions, number of directors and any restrictions on activities. The articles must be signed by each incorporator and, if applicable, be in French or bilingual.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney or authorizing resolution if incorporator is a legal entity
Notice of registered office (if submitted separately)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon a notice of deficiency, amend the articles and resubmit within the prescribed period; seek written reasons and, where necessary, request reconsideration by the Registraire.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic submission, fee payment and issuance of certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec secure online incorporation service (Déclaration de constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Registraire's Quebec online portal, upload the executed articles, pay the applicable filing fee by credit card or interac, and submit the application. Monitor the file; upon approval, obtain the certificate of incorporation and the assigned enterprise/incorporation number.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity of initial directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or suspended, review the Registraire's reasons, cure all deficiencies and electronically resubmit the corrected filing, or institute judicial review before the competent court if the rejection is contested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational meeting and first board resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office of the Corporation and the Board of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene an organizational board meeting. Adopt By-law No. 1 (general corporate by-law), elect officers, approve the issuance of shares to subscribers, and record the statutory first board resolution in the corporate minute book. Ensure the register of directors and officers is completed.
required_dossiers: Share subscription agreements and share certificates
Written consents to act from each director and officer
Minute book and corporate register (bilingual or French)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any consent or meeting document is incomplete, obtain a signed written resolution in lieu of a meeting within 30 days, retroactively validating the organizational decision, subject to applicable law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registrations with CRA and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Business Number (BN) registration via CRA's online services. Register for GST/HST, Quebec sales tax (QST), corporate income tax and, if applicable, payroll deductions accounts. Provide Revenu Québec with the incorporation certificate and officer information to obtain the QST certificate and account number.
required_dossiers: Personal information of directors/officers (e.g., social insurance number, residential address)
Bank account confirmation and legal entity identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax account registration is delayed or incomplete, contact Revenu Québec's dedicated business services line or CRA business inquiries to reconcile information and expedite account issuance; provide supplemental documents if requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate records maintenance and annual regulatory filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec and the Corporation's registered records office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, maintain up-to-date share register, director register, officer register, and minute book. Deliver any required information to the Registraire, including director changes and annual returns, to preserve the corporation's existence and good standing.
required_dossiers: Annual return form (Déclaration de mise à jour annuelle)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a filing is flagged or late fees are assessed, file the missing or corrected declaration immediately, request penalty cancellation on reasonable grounds, and maintain proof of submission for audit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not required – an electronic B2B marketplace store under ISIC 4791 does not constitute industrial or physical manufacturing activity in Quebec; no specific industrial licensing board issues an operating permit for this activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: N/A – no statutory operating or manufacturing licence is required for a pure online B2B wholesale platform.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques (MELCC) – Quebec Ministry of the Environment, the Fight Against Climate Change
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no EIA registration or full report is required because no physical construction, wastewater discharge or significant pollutant emission is generated by an online marketplace. If a warehouse is subsequently added, screening under Quebec's environmental authorization framework may apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A for the online platform operation. If the corporation later operates a physical warehouse or logistics centre, it must comply with municipal by-laws and MELCC standards relating to wastewater, VOCs and solid waste handling as applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for a purely digital business. If the corporation leases an office or coworking space, the commercial landlord's certificate of occupation covers fire and structural safety; the employer must nevertheless register the workplace with CNESST and post occupational health and safety notices as prescribed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agence du revenu du Québec (ARQ) for provincial taxes including QST and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal taxes including corporate income tax; official portals ark.gouv.qc.ca and canada.ca/revenue-agency
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Domestic business corporations obtain a federal Business Number (BN) as statutory TIN through CRA online registration using Form RC1 or equivalent, accompanied by articles of incorporation, proof of legal status, and registered office address. Quebec entities additionally register with ARQ for provincial tax IDs and QST obligations via the ARQ portal with supporting corporate documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available under Canadian tax law. Hybrid mismatch and treaty shopping rules enforced through Income Tax Act provisions and GAAR to prevent artificial tax outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/QST (Goods and Services Tax / Quebec Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API reporting, or digital stamping requirements for standard GST/QST. Voluntary electronic invoicing permitted; B2B marketplace operators must register for GST/HST if annual taxable supplies exceed threshold and comply with platform transaction reporting obligations under CRA rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Canada or services supplied to non-residents outside Canada qualify for zero-rated GST/HST treatment. Eligibility requires proof that goods left Canada and recipient is non-resident with no benefit in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Failure to substantiate export results in GST/HST reassessment, penalties of 10-50 percent of tax due, and interest. Fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger criminal prosecution, full tax clawback, and director liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains free current account convertibility with no restrictions on profit remittances or dividends for resident corporations. Capital account transactions are subject to voluntary reporting to the Bank of Canada via the International Data Reporting System (IDRS) for amounts exceeding CAD 10,000. Profit repatriation requires tax clearance and beneficial ownership verification but needs no prior approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds under Canadian law. Exporters retain full discretion over foreign exchange utilization. All export sales must be reported to the Canada Revenue Agency on Form T2125. Significant transactions may trigger optional Bank of Canada reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech platforms such as Wise, Stripe Treasury, and Revolut Business offer viable cross-border payment and treasury services. Regulatory licensing under Canada's Payment Services Act and OSFI oversight limits full EMI operations. Traditional commercial banks remain primary for integrated FX hedging and liquidity clearing due to comprehensive compliance frameworks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Corporate account opening in Quebec permits remote KYC via digital platforms for standard clients. In-person interviews or appearances may be mandated for directors in cases of high-risk profiles, large transaction volumes, or enhanced due diligence requirements under federal AML legislation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive source of funds and source of wealth affidavits, corporate resolutions, and independent legal opinions
Up-to-date share registers, notarized ownership declarations, and verification of ultimate controllers
Documented commercial rationale, trade agreements, and third-party confirmations

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from non-resident shareholders are processed via SWIFT wire transfers with purpose codes including 'CAPCON' for capital contributions or 'EQUITY' for equity investments. All inbound wires require supporting documentation such as shareholder agreements, board minutes, and proof of legitimate funds origin. Amounts exceeding CAD 10,000 trigger Bank of Canada reporting obligations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements are facilitated through SWIFT MT103 messages or commercial letters of credit. Purpose codes such as 'PAYMENT' or 'TRADE SETTLEMENT' are used. Quebec corporations must comply with GST/HST invoicing requirements and anti-money laundering controls for all cross-border disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX contracts for fixed future exchange rates
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for hedging without principal exchange
Currency swap agreements for multi-currency funding
FX options for premium-based protection against adverse movements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal and Quebec general corporate income tax rate (15% federal Part I general rate + 11.5% Quebec provincial general rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction for Canadian-controlled private corporations: reduced federal rate of 9% plus Quebec reduced rate of 3.2% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits; Quebec innovation and productivity tax credits; no statutory tax holidays or territorial exemptions in Canada.
